title: Excavations in Palestine and Trans-Jordan, 1937-8: Sanctuary of the Visitation, 'Ain Karim
author: (round-up; clearance by the Custody of the Holy Land)
screen_term: 'ain karim (spelling of gazetteer 'ein kerem'); paragraph without its own heading
location_note: Sanctuary of the Visitation, 'Ain Karim; placed by name.
notes: Clearance March-June 1938: earlier building under the crypt with a spring gallery cut in the cliff, later crypt and church with halls, a plastered chamber in the courtyard (called 'the cistern' in the finds list) with glass and 'channel-nozzle' lamps, Arab-type glazed sherds near the surface; a rain-water catch-basin before the church. No dates given for the water features.

features.subtype: gallery cut into the cliff to a spring, masonry-faced and vaulted; clay-pipe drain carrying the spring overflow from a plastered well out of the building
features.period: earlier than the crypt and church; not dated
features.quote: A drain made of clay pipes, placed on the native clay, traversed

features.subtype: plastered chamber about 7 m square (crushed-sherd plaster), called 'the cistern'
features.period: not dated (glass and channel-nozzle lamps in the fill)
features.quote: immediately on the pavement of the cistern two glass lamps
a catch-basin for collecting rain water
